facts.text: St. Anthony was founded in 1888 by members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter‑day Saints, though some say 1890.
The city’s name honors Saint Anthony Falls in Minnesota, the largest waterfall on the Mississippi River.
In 1909, St. Anthony built its first county courthouse, and two years later opened a cinema that screened silent films.
David Thompson established a fur trading post at the confluence of Henry’s Fork and the Snake River, marking early European presence.
The town’s sandy dunes along Henry’s Fork offer year‑round recreation, from cross‑country skiing in winter to dune bashing in summer.
St. Anthony’s historic downtown features the Silver Horseshoe Inn, a preserved building that reflects the town’s early 20th‑century architecture.
